newsitem.title: FRANCE: Giscard says room for French rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Giscard says room for French rate cuts.

text.p: Former French president Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Tuesday there was room for lower interest rates in France and that the markets understood German rates would have to be cut "sooner or later".
"In France, we can continue to reduce our rates by a reasonable margin," Giscard said in an interview with French daily Le Figaro.

He said he did not think French rate cuts would have any destabilising effect and the financial markets would react favourably. When the Germans saw that everything was fine, they "will be able to take their turn to do something."
Giscard also welcomed the fact the dollar had risen to 5.50 against the franc, a level he called for on November 20 when the franc was at 5.08 against the U.S. currency.
"It's a pleasing element which will help our economic situation and allow an improvement in employment," he said.
The dollar had appreciated sharply during the past two months because there had been a shift in sentiment, he said.
He said it was apparent that Germany faced difficulties with unemployment and that its economic situation had deteriorated during the last few months.
"The markets have understood that, sooner or later, German rates would have to be lowered," Giscard said.
